clue.text: Doesn't like being snapped at?

parts.note: snapped means photographed, not spoken to sharply: someone who shrinks from the lens

explanation.surface: Someone touchy who hates being spoken to sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapped at' reads as being barked at, but a snap is a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A person reluctant to be photographed is described by this compound adjective.

clue.text: A light rubber staged for Christmas?

definitions.text: A light rubber staged for Christmas?

parts.words: A light rubber staged for Christmas?
parts.note: the hero of a festive pantomime who rubs a magic lamp, a light, to call up a genie

explanation.surface: A gentle masseur putting on a show at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage tradition; this hero rubs a lamp, so he is a 'light rubber'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pantomime's title character summons the genie by rubbing a lamp, and the show is staged each Christmas.

clue.text: Quickly get it off the printing machine

parts.note: ex means out of or off, as in ex-works
a press is a printing machine

explanation.surface: Someone asked to grab a copy fast from the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending something by fast delivery is sending it this way, so the word stands for speedily.

clue.text: Supporting a bad habit some say

parts.note: gambling is what some people would call a bad habit

explanation.surface: Someone excusing a vice by saying it is only a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiding or encouraging someone, especially in wrongdoing, is backing them.

clue.text: Roy embroiled with Ned over there

indicators.note: embroiled means tangled up, so the letters of the two names are mixed together

explanation.surface: Two men, Roy and Ned, fighting somewhere in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: An old or literary word meaning at that distant place.

clue.text: Potentially great quote about a mere fag

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to quote is to cite

indicators.note: potentially says the word great could become something else, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone talking up a grand quotation about a mere smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially great' looks like praise for the quote, but 'Potentially' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container. In British slang a fag is a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a fag is a smoke rolled in paper.

clue.text: No republic contribution to backing dominions

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark on supporting the self-governing parts of an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a monarch is by nature not a republic.

clue.text: One of the ladies to be seen in a toss-up

definitions.text: One of the ladies to be seen in a toss-up

parts.words: One of the ladies to be seen in a toss-up
parts.note: a seated female figure printed on old British coins, so she shows up when a coin is tossed

explanation.surface: A woman visible in a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The helmeted female figure symbolising Britain appeared on British pennies, so she turns up in a coin toss.
explanation.definitionFit: The female personification of Britain appeared on coins, which are flipped to decide a toss-up.

clue.text: A peer of many parts

parts.note: a lord who was a famous actor and played many roles

explanation.surface: A versatile member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier, the great English actor, was made a life peer; parts are stage roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence, the celebrated stage and screen actor, became a baron and played countless roles.

clue.text: It can be folded away for the rest of the Scouts' holiday

definitions.text: It can be folded away for the rest of the Scouts' holiday

parts.words: It can be folded away for the rest of the Scouts' holiday
parts.note: rest means sleep, not the remainder: a collapsible bed used under canvas

explanation.surface: Packing up the gear for the remainder of a Scout trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest of' reads as 'the remainder of', but rest is sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A light folding bed is what campers such as Scouts sleep on.

clue.text: Pull a measure of liquid

definitions.meaning: a draw or haul, as of a net or a load
a dose or swallow of drink

explanation.surface: Tugging on a beer pump to pour a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hauling action and a swallow of drink, as in beer on tap.

clue.text: It's supposed to pay to set a driveway out

indicators.note: way out means wild or crazy, so the letters of the words before are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Advice that laying a new driveway is a good investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan ran 'drive way' together; 'way out' is the anagram signal for SET A DRIVE. The definition plays on the saying 'it pays to advertise'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says publicity pays, so promoting a product is what is supposed to bring in money.

clue.text: Having struggled under the highway rent

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another is written after it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a highway
rent and riven both mean torn apart

explanation.surface: Someone who fought hard to pay rent beneath a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for housing, but it is the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of strive, meaning having made great efforts.

clue.text: Robert undressed, but on the right side of the blanket!

definitions.text: on the right side of the blanket

indicators.note: dressed means arranged or put in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, split off the front of undressed

explanation.surface: Robert stripped off, but he is legitimate.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'undressed' as 'un' plus 'dressed', the anagram signal. 'Born on the wrong side of the blanket' is an old British phrase for illegitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born on the right side of the blanket means legitimate birth to married parents, which is the idea of being genuinely of a line.

clue.text: Punk centre is getting no return from one sound

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the middle of punk
return means the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: A punk at the heart of things gets no reply from a lone noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Voices together on a single note are in harmony with a lone pitch.

clue.text: Superior worker's advantage

parts.note: superior and upper both mean higher
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A higher-grade employee has the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the dominant position, control or the edge in a contest.

clue.text: Hops over the floor for oven building

definitions.text: Hops over the floor for oven building

parts.words: Hops over the floor for oven building
parts.note: hops are the plant crop, spread on a floor above a kiln to dry; the building holds that oven

explanation.surface: Dancing around while an oven is built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hops' suggests jumping, but it is the crop used in brewing; in Kent they are dried in a round brick kiln with a pointed cowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops, a building with a heated floor where the crop is laid out.

clue.text: Not a word for a win, by the way

parts.note: a gain is a win or profit
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone saying, by the way, that this is no word for victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the answer meaning the opposite of 'for', so 'Not' stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposed to, the reverse of being in favour, so the word works as a negation.

clue.text: Point to one who impresses and makes a quick run

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun, one who makes a quick run

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
a printer presses ink onto paper, impressing it

explanation.surface: Pointing to someone who makes an impression and then dashes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who' serves both halves: one who impresses, and one who makes a quick run.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who races over short distances at top speed.

clue.text: A dozen trying folk ought to reach it eventually

definitions.text: A dozen trying folk ought to reach it eventually

parts.words: A dozen trying folk ought to reach it eventually
parts.note: trying means judging a case, not tiresome: the twelve jurors must finally decide

explanation.surface: Twelve annoying people should get somewhere in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying folk' sounds like tiresome people; a jury of twelve tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's final decision on guilt is what twelve jurors work towards.

clue.text: Small change in Spanish fashion

parts.note: small change means a coin, the money once used in Spain, not a minor alteration in style

explanation.surface: A slight shift in what is fashionable in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' reads as alteration and 'fashion' as style, but the clue means the coins Spain used before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's currency unit before the euro.

clue.text: A course fora specialised class of Marines

indicators.note: class means sort into order, so a special sorting of the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A training course for an elite group of Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specialised class of' rearranges MARINES.
explanation.definitionFit: A short course of study or meeting for discussion, held for a small group of students.

clue.text: Great pains taken to get at the truth maybe

definitions.text: Great pains taken to get at the truth maybe

parts.words: Great pains taken to get at the truth maybe
parts.note: pains means suffering inflicted, not effort: agony used in interrogation

explanation.surface: Someone working very hard to find out the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great pains taken' sounds like diligent effort, but it is suffering inflicted to extract a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflicting severe suffering, often to force a confession.

clue.text: Smooth movement at sea as the sun goes down

parts.note: even and smooth both mean level
the tide is the rise and fall of the sea

explanation.surface: Calm waters at sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word for evening, the time of sunset.

clue.text: Miserable crowd over what was once Simla

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece over another is written before it

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crowd

indicators.note: what was once says the letters of Simla were formerly in another arrangement, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A gloomy crowd gathered at the former name of an Indian hill town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what was once' rearranges SIMLA into ISMAL. Simla is the old spelling of Shimla, a hill station in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and depressing, causing low spirits.

clue.text: In business, a little training system for hospital

parts.note: a firm is a business
RY is the short form of railway, a system of trains

explanation.surface: Inside a company, a small course of instruction for a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training system' is a railway, a system of trains, not instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where the sick are cared for, an old name for a hospital.

clue.text: Frightful house; I'd move

indicators.note: move means shift around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who finds their house awful and wants to relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly or horrible, as in shockingly unpleasant.

clue.text: Could it knock out England shortly in its quick-firing fashion?

definitions.text: Could it knock out England shortly in its quick-firing fashion?

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to stun is to knock out
ENG is the short form of England

explanation.surface: Could a quick-firing team knock England out cheaply?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the light automatic weapon while 'in' puts ENG into STUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A light submachine weapon used by the British in the Second World War, able to stun with rapid fire.

clue.text: A coin is tossed over island capital in dispute

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Flipping a coin to settle an island's argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital of Cyprus is divided between Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The divided capital of Cyprus, split between rival communities.

clue.text: Branches whose leaves are bound to be widely distributed

definitions.text: Branches whose leaves are bound to be widely distributed

parts.words: Branches whose leaves are bound to be widely distributed
parts.note: branches are local offices and leaves are pages in bound books lent out widely

explanation.surface: Trees whose foliage is sure to scatter far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' and 'leaves' suggest trees, but these are local lending offices whose books are bound and circulated.
explanation.definitionFit: Branch buildings lending bound books out to readers across a town.
